messages.content: Can you use the get_stock_prices function to retrieve the stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Tesla over the duration of 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, and 1 month respectively?

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call the get_stock_prices function with companies ["Apple", "Microsoft", "Amazon", "Tesla"] and durations ["1 week", "2 weeks", "3 weeks", "1 month"]. The function signature expects an object with keys companies (string[]) and duration (string). But we have multiple durations per company. The function only accepts one duration at a time. We need to decide how to handle this. Possibly we can make separate calls for each pair. Or maybe we can combine them into a single request if the API supports multiple durations? The function spec says "Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc." It doesn't say it can accept multiple durations. So likely we need to make four separate calls.

We should ask clarifying question: do they want separate calls or combined? They said "retrieve the stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Tesla over the duration of 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, and 1 month respectively?" That implies mapping: Apple -> 1 week, Microsoft -> 2 weeks, Amazon -> 3 weeks, Tesla -> 1 month. So we need to call get_stock_prices four times with appropriate parameters.

Thus we will call get_stock_prices with companies ["Apple"], duration "1 week". Then ["Microsoft"], "2 weeks". Then ["Amazon"], "3 weeks". Then ["Tesla"], "1 month".

We'll produce four calls.
